predecessors.name: Ghana Empire
predecessors.text: Wagadu and Koumbi Saleh, taken from the Ghana kings 'by 1203'

successors.name: Mali Empire
successors.text: 'When the Soso empire collapsed, the entire Kaniaga region was incorporated into Sundiata's Mali Empire'

ledger.x: c. 1200-1203: the Sosso, a clan of slaves of the Ghana kings, take Wagadu. 'Capture of Wagadu: c. 1200'; 'an event that Heinrich Barth dated to approximately 1203'; the Mali page has Soumaoro Kante 'came to power' in 1203. Cliopatria's 1202 start is kept.

c. 1200-1203: the Sosso take Wagadu from the Ghana kings. after a civil war weakened the state it 'became easy prey for Soumaoro Kante'. The Sosso page does not say Koumbi Saleh was taken; the Ghana page does ('Diara Kante took control of Koumbi Saleh').
Undated, before Kirina: Soumaoro Kante subdues the Mandinka chieftaincies of the Manden.
ledger.cp: Mandinka chieftaincies of the Manden (no state named by the page)

ledger.x: c. 1235: Sundiata Keita defeats Soumaoro at Kirina and takes the Sosso lands. 'At the Battle of Kirina (c. 1235) the Mandinka prince Sundiata Keita led a coalition of smaller states to soundly defeat the Sosso and kill Soumaoro'; 'the entire Kaniaga region was incorporated into Sundiata's Mali Empire'.

c. 1235: Sundiata destroys Sosso. 'Sundiata marched on Sosso itself and destroyed it, marking the kingdom's end.' Survivors went west into Senegambia or south into Futa Jallon (ancestors of the Susu and Yalunka).

wars.name: Sosso conquest of Ghana
wars.outcome: The Sosso took Wagadu from the Ghana kings (infobox c.

wars.name: Soumaoro Kante's wars on the Manding chiefdoms
wars.outcome: The Sosso subdued the Mandinka chieftaincies to the south until Sundiata's rising.

wars.name: Battle of Kirina
wars.outcome: Sundiata Keita's coalition defeated the Sosso and killed Soumaoro; Sosso was destroyed and Kaniaga passed to Mali.

certainty.note: Oral-history polity; the page warns that oral histories 'can compress events and people from different periods into single narratives'.
